thesis: Hold. Sizing equity is $1000.14, cash is $750.01, and the only position is VTI at a $250.13 mark (about 25% of equity), inside the 8% cash floor, the 45% single-name cap, and the 7-position limit. This tick's new facts conflict. August consumer spending snapped back, while the Fed's main inflation gauge rose sharply in August and that piece ties the print to a rate hike earlier this month, the first in three years. Hotter inflation plus a completed hike is not a clean add to equity beta at the open, and VIX at 15.81 (down 1.43% as of 05:00Z) is not a reason to sell the existing VTI sleeve. I will not buy TLT: the 10-year is still 5.230%, and the inflation headline outweighs a strategist's comment that a roughly 5.25% yield cushion makes Treasuries attractive; the last supplied TLT mark was 78.23, down 0.50% as of 2026-09-29T04:00:00Z. I will not buy USO: WTI 91.01 (+1.82%) and USO 147.08 (+2.60%), both as of 04:00Z, are price context without a new fundamental in this pack. The Rosenblatt note on Amazon, the Meta enterprise column, and Citi's sell on Moderna are opinion; I do not hold MRNA and cannot short. DigitalBridge's 8-K (items 2.01, 3.01, and 5.01, published 13:29Z) includes a delisting or listing notice and a change in control, so I stay out. Other 8-Ks are item codes without terms. Carryover on junk-bond stress, weak breadth, and soft hiring is not a fresh catalyst to rotate. Keep VTI and the cash buffer. Proposal only; no fill assumed.
